summary: Repaired writer.py and verified SIGHUP rotation, deleted-descriptor release, continued writing under the same PID, clean SIGTERM exit, archive preservation, and persistence across a node restart.
actions_performed: Installed a Python 3-compatible writer with SIGHUP and SIGTERM handlers.
On SIGHUP, the writer opens the current audit.log, switches streams, and closes the old descriptor.
On SIGTERM, the writer exits through a finally block and closes its log.
Preserved audit event A101 and archived event A100; the archive checksum remained unchanged.
Safely restarted node1 and repeated the complete functional test after recovery.

evidence.summary: Shows the installed signal-handling source, successful syntax validation, executable permissions, and unchanged archive checksum.

evidence.requirement: SIGHUP releases the deleted descriptor and continues on the current path without restarting
evidence.summary: The live writer initially held audit.log (deleted); after SIGHUP the same process identity referenced the replacement inode, had no deleted descriptor, and continued increasing the current file.

evidence.requirement: SIGTERM closes the log and exits cleanly
evidence.summary: Controlled SIGTERM tests returned exit status 0 with empty stderr and no remaining writer process.

evidence.requirement: Existing archive and audit records preserved
evidence.summary: Event A100 remained in archive/previous.log with its original SHA-256 checksum; current event A101 also remained present.

evidence.requirement: Installed OS release and kernel retained
evidence.summary: Ubuntu 24.04 and kernel 6.8.0-71-generic were unchanged before and after repair/restart.

Healthy baseline boot ID 37344ae4-6582-4c1f-ac5c-fcb32f67b968 was captured, safe reboot acknowledgement returned, the recovered boot ID changed to 6a3a56b3-5666-438f-b86a-2c74291bcd7e, and post-restart data plus complete SIGHUP/SIGTERM behavior passed.
